research.question: Which purpose-built memory database or graph memory layer should COAT use for durable agent memories across distributed fork/join workflows?
research.answer: The captured source set supports using Zep/Graphiti over MCP as the default temporal graph memory layer, with Qdrant as the embedded retrieval mirror and Restate remaining the execution journal. This replay fixture validates the parser and validator contract only; it does not refresh source freshness.

sources.title: Zep Key Concepts
sources.quote: Graph RAG, agent memory, and context assembly
sources.summary: Zep documents a knowledge graph, context block, fact invalidation, graph search, and agentic tool use for memory retrieval.

sources.title: Graphiti MCP Server
sources.summary: Graphiti exposes temporal graph memory over MCP with HTTP transport and supports FalkorDB or Neo4j backends.

sources.title: Qdrant API and SDKs
sources.summary: Qdrant documents official SDKs, REST and gRPC APIs, and Rust client support for production vector memory.

facts_to_use: Default memory_policy.store.kind should be zep_graphiti when temporal graph memory is enabled.
Default memory_policy.vector.store.kind should be qdrant for embedded retrieval.
Expose Graphiti as an MCP memory server rather than embedding memory logic inside the coordinator.
facts_to_avoid: Do not treat vector-only storage as sufficient for temporal fork/join agent memory.
Do not treat this replay fixture as proof that sources are still current.

proposed_goal_updates.recommendation: Set the default memory store kind to zep_graphiti for semantic agent memory.
proposed_goal_updates.reason: The captured sources favor a temporal graph memory layer for fork/join context rather than vector-only retrieval.
